cards.front: fair test
cards.back: A test where only one thing is changed and everything else stays the same.
cards.say: fair test. A test where only one thing is changed and everything else stays the same.

cards.front: variable
cards.back: Something that can change in a test.
cards.say: variable. Something that can change in a test.

cards.front: What do we change in a fair test?
cards.back: Only one thing.
cards.say: What do we change in a fair test? Only one thing.

cards.front: What do we keep the same in a fair test?
cards.back: Everything else, such as the amount, size and time.
cards.say: What do we keep the same in a fair test? Everything else, such as the amount, size and time.

cards.front: measure
cards.back: To find out how big, long, heavy or hot something is, using a number and a unit.
cards.say: measure. To find out how big, long, heavy or hot something is, using a number and a unit.

cards.front: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a pencil?
cards.back: Centimetres (cm).
cards.say: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a pencil? Centimetres (cm).

cards.front: Which unit would you use to measure the mass of an apple?
cards.back: Grams (g).
cards.say: Which unit would you use to measure the mass of an apple? Grams (g).

cards.front: Which unit would you use to measure the temperature of water?
cards.back: Degrees Celsius.
cards.say: Which unit would you use to measure the temperature of water? Degrees Celsius.

cards.front: Which unit would you use to measure water in a jug?
cards.back: Millilitres (ml) or litres (l).
cards.say: Which unit would you use to measure water in a jug? Millilitres (ml) or litres (l).

cards.front: Which unit would you use to time a short race?
cards.back: Seconds.
cards.say: Which unit would you use to time a short race? Seconds.

cards.front: Which tool measures length?
cards.back: A ruler or a tape measure.
cards.say: Which tool measures length? A ruler or a tape measure.

cards.front: Which tool measures mass?
cards.back: Scales or a balance.
cards.say: Which tool measures mass? Scales or a balance.

cards.front: Which tool measures temperature?
cards.back: A thermometer.
cards.say: Which tool measures temperature? A thermometer.

cards.front: Which tool measures the volume of a liquid?
cards.back: A measuring cylinder or measuring jug.
cards.say: Which tool measures the volume of a liquid? A measuring cylinder or measuring jug.

cards.front: Which tool measures time?
cards.back: A stopwatch or a timer.
cards.say: Which tool measures time? A stopwatch or a timer.

cards.front: Why do we repeat a measurement?
cards.back: To check the result is reliable and to spot mistakes.
cards.say: Why do we repeat a measurement? To check the result is reliable and to spot mistakes.

cards.front: prediction
cards.back: What you think will happen, and why, before you test.
cards.say: prediction. What you think will happen, and why, before you test.

cards.front: Why is it not a fair test if one plant gets more water and more light?
cards.back: Two things are changed, so you cannot tell which one made the difference.
cards.say: Why is it not a fair test if one plant gets more water and more light? Two things are changed, so you cannot tell which one made the difference.

cards.front: You test which paper towel soaks up most water. What do you keep the same?
cards.back: The size of the paper towel, the amount of water and the time.
cards.say: You test which paper towel soaks up most water. What do you keep the same? The size of the paper towel, the amount of water and the time.

cards.front: You test which paper towel soaks up most water. What do you change?
cards.back: The type of paper towel.
cards.say: You test which paper towel soaks up most water. What do you change? The type of paper towel.

cards.front: Which is a better measurement, "about a cup" or "250 ml"?
cards.back: 250 ml. A number with a unit is more exact.
cards.say: Which is a better measurement, "about a cup" or "250 ml"? 250 ml. A number with a unit is more exact.

cards.front: Why do we write down our results?
cards.back: So we can compare them and see what happened.
cards.say: Why do we write down our results? So we can compare them and see what happened.

cards.front: Where should an object start when you measure it with a ruler?
cards.back: At the zero mark at the start of the ruler.
cards.say: Where should an object start when you measure it with a ruler? At the zero mark at the start of the ruler.

cards.front: Where should your eye be when you read a measuring jug?
cards.back: Level with the line, looking straight at it.
cards.say: Where should your eye be when you read a measuring jug? Level with the line, looking straight at it.
